page: Microsoft Azure E4pds_v6 is an ARM-based memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 hardware, offering 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz. Its processor architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a large 128 MB L3 cache. System memory measures 32.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-core density of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage capabilities include a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD alongside support for Premium Storage. The configuration contains no dedicated GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmarking reflects an architecture tuned primarily for memory throughput and data movement rather than complex vector math. The instance achieves a top-tier score in PassMark memory testing, accompanied by 85.02 GB/s in uncached large-block read operations. Compression efficiency is strong, with single-threaded gzip throughput reaching 32.9 GB/s. Application tests confirm stable performance for web traffic and caching, delivering 7.84 GB/sec in static web serving and 8.02 million operations per second in Redis SET routines. Conversely, compute benchmarks show lower scores in PassMark encryption, extended instructions, ray tracing, and LLM text generation, stemming from the absence of advanced x86 vector extensions.

The hardware configuration provides strong qualitative cost efficiency by leveraging power-efficient ARM Neoverse-N2 cores to deliver substantial memory capacity without the premium overhead of excessive vCPU counts. Bundled local NVMe storage reduces external disk dependency for temporary data files and caches. The system is well fitted for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, relational database engines, stream processing, and extract-transform-load (ETL) data pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E4pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on 64-bit ARM Neoverse-N2 architecture, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz alongside 32.0 GB of system memory and a 236 GB local NVMe SSD. Featuring an 8.0 GB per-core memory ratio and 128 MB of L3 cache, the system targets workloads requiring high memory density. Benchmark testing demonstrates exceptional memory subsystem efficiency with a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3017.40 and robust single-threaded gzip compression at 32.9 GB/s. In-memory data structures perform reliably, achieving 8.02 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.84 GB/s static web throughput. However, compute performance in cryptographic and vector workloads drops to lower tiers due to lack of x86-specific extensions. Offering qualitative resource efficiency through ARM-based power scaling and integrated scratch storage, the E4pds_v6 is suited for in-memory caches, database servers, and memory-bound ETL workflows.
